name: Peter Zaffino
current_role: Global Head of Financial Services, Palantir Technologies (from Sept 2026); former Chairman & CEO / Executive Chair of AIG
profile: Insurance executive (b. 1967) who spent 16 years at Marsh & McLennan (CEO of Guy Carpenter 2008-11, CEO of Marsh 2011-17) before joining AIG as COO in 2017. AIG CEO from 2021 and chairman from 2022, credited with its underwriting turnaround; handed CEO role to Eric Andersen June 2026 and left the board Sept 15, 2026 to join Palantir.
interesting_fact: At AIG's 2025 Investor Day he hosted a panel on generative AI in underwriting with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Palantir CEO Alex Karp - and in 2026 left AIG to join Palantir.
deep_cut_fact: He played collegiate soccer as a goalkeeper at Boston College (BA economics, 1989), and began his insurance career at The Hartford before a GE Capital alternative-risk unit.
notes: Very recent move from AIG to Palantir (announced Sept 2, 2026; WSJ/Insurance Journal). Best route is Palantir communications/IR. Energy/data-center angle: AI adoption in insurance.

name: David Scott Offer
current_role: Executive Vice President & General Counsel, Flex Ltd.
profile: Goes by Scott Offer. UK- and US-qualified lawyer (LSE law degree) who started at London firm Boodle Hatfield, spent years at Motorola (chief counsel of Motorola Mobility under Google), then was SVP & GC of Lenovo before joining Flex in 2016, where he leads legal, government relations, IP, compliance and security.
interesting_fact: Named by the Financial Times Innovative Lawyers programme (2025) as one of the Top 20 General Counsel of the last two decades; his team ran the separation of solar-tracker maker Nextracker from Flex, one of the largest US IPOs of 2023.
deep_cut_fact: He has written on Flex's blog about measuring corporate ethics with data, e.g. 'A scorecard approach to improve compliance and ethics across the enterprise' (Aug 2022) and 'Data-backed ethical culture' (Jan 2022).
notes: Known professionally as Scott Offer. Data-center angle: Flex is big in data-center power/liquid cooling and announced (May 2026) intent to spin off its Cloud & Power Infrastructure segment.

name: Ned S Holmes
current_role: Independent Director (Compensation Committee Chair), Prosperity Bancshares; Chairman & CEO, Ned S. Holmes Investments, Inc.
profile: Houston-born banker and real estate investor (age 81 per 2026 proxy). Chaired Commercial Bancshares (1991-2001) until its merger into Prosperity Bancshares, then chaired Prosperity 2001-06 and remains a director. Has run Ned S. Holmes Investments since 1976 and led Parkway Investments/Texas (1980-2005), managing Houston real estate.
interesting_fact: Served on the Texas Transportation Commission (2007-2012) and is Chairman Emeritus of the Greater Houston Partnership; also a former director of Memorial Hermann, Baylor College of Medicine and MD Anderson.
deep_cut_fact: Through Parkway Investments/Texas he managed the San Diego Princess Hotel (a resort on Mission Bay) among his special real-estate projects, and he served on the Gulf Coast Rail District board.
notes: Low public profile; no personal web/social presence found. Route via Prosperity Bancshares IR (media/IR contact on releases: Cullen Zalman) or Greater Houston Partnership.

name: Andrea Pfeifer
current_role: Honorary Chair of the Board, Advisor and Co-Chair of the Scientific Advisory Board, AC Immune SA (retired as CEO June 2026)
profile: German-born scientist (PhD toxicology, Wurzburg) who headed Nestle's global research in Lausanne, then co-founded Alzheimer's/neurodegeneration biotech AC Immune in 2003 and led it as CEO for 23 years, including its 2016 Nasdaq IPO. Retired as CEO at the June 2026 AGM; remains honorary chair and adviser and is active in the Davos Alzheimer's Collaborative.
interesting_fact: At Nestle she led the scientific development of LC1, described as the first functional food, and co-founded the Nestle venture capital fund; she is one of the longest-serving female CEOs in biotech.
deep_cut_fact: As an NIH/NCI postdoc (1984-89) in Curtis Harris's lab she helped create early immortalized human lung and liver cell lines still licensed for research; of NIH she said: 'It was an incredible experience, the openness and sharing. I've never seen anything like that again.'

public_contacts.value: inquiry@davosalzheimerscollaborative.com (Davos Alzheimer's Collaborative, of which she is a member)

notes: Retired as CEO June 11, 2026 citing family time; Chair Martin Zugel became interim CEO. Best route: AC Immune general/IR contact. Based in Lausanne, Switzerland.

name: Jennifer K Mann
current_role: Senior Advisor, The Coca-Cola Company (EVP & President, North America Operating Unit 2023-July 2026); director, Verizon Communications
profile: 29-year Coca-Cola veteran with an accounting degree from Georgia State. Rose through commercial, customer and marketing roles, served as chief people officer and chief of staff to CEO James Quincey, ran Global Ventures, then led the North America operating unit (US and Canada, Coke's largest) 2023-July 2026; now a senior advisor and Verizon board member.
interesting_fact: As president of Coca-Cola's Global Ventures she led the company's investments in Costa Coffee and Monster Beverage.
deep_cut_fact: Earlier in her career she held leadership roles on Coca-Cola Freestyle (the touchscreen custom-mix fountain machine) and on the McDonald's customer team; she has served on boards of Morehouse College and Ronald McDonald House Charities.
notes: Transitioned out of operating role July 2026; now senior advisor. Web search quota ran out mid-lane, so research relied on the official Coca-Cola bio.

name: David Joseph Meyer
current_role: Chairman of the Board (co-founder; CEO until Feb 2024), Titan Machinery Inc.
profile: North Dakota entrepreneur who co-founded Titan Machinery in Wahpeton in 1980 by buying out a Case farm-equipment dealership, grew it through acquisitions (notably the 2003 C.I. Farm Power merger) and took it public in 2007 with 34 stores. Titan is now a multi-billion-dollar Case IH/New Holland dealer network across the US, Europe and Australia; Meyer handed the CEO role to Bryan Knutson in 2024 and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Titan grew from a single Wahpeton, ND farm store to a Nasdaq-listed dealer group with $2B+ in revenue and stores in the US, Europe and Australia.
deep_cut_fact: Right out of college in 1975 he joined Case Corporation as a product specialist for 4WD tractors, then that November went to work at the Meyer-Jones Farm Store in Wahpeton - the dealership he and partner Darrell Larson later bought to form Titan; they opened a second store in Lisbon, ND in 1977.
notes: Based in West Fargo, ND. Ag-equipment angle rather than energy; no personal social presence found. Web search quota ran out mid-lane; relied on Wikipedia and company IR site.

name: Fredric H Gould
current_role: Vice Chairman of the Board, One Liberty Properties; Director, BRT Apartments Corp.
profile: Long Island real-estate investor (age 90 per April 2026 proxy) with 50+ years in the business. Patriarch of the Gould family real-estate group: chaired One Liberty Properties 1989-2013 (now vice chairman), chaired BRT Apartments 1984-2013, led Georgetown Partners (managing GP of Gould Investors L.P.). One Liberty has repositioned to an 80%+ industrial REIT; his sons Matthew and Jeffrey lead the family businesses.
interesting_fact: One Liberty, the REIT he chaired for 24 years, has shifted from ~40% industrial assets in 2018 to over 80% industrial in 2026 - and Gould himself sat on the board of industrial REIT EastGroup Properties from 1998 to 2019.
